claims.text: Mechanical sliding produces severe plastic deformation and an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer in CoCrFeMnNi.
The sliding-generated near-surface layer is partially amorphous.
The ultra-nanocrystalline or amorphous surface state promotes rapid and uniform formation of a dense, chemically stable passive oxide film.
The dynamically generated surface structure and passive film synergistically reduce both wear and corrosion rates.
CoCrFeMnNi is initially a single-phase HEA.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi material is coarse-grained.
An AlCoCrFeNiMoTi alloy with an optimized B addition is a coarse-grained microalloyed variant suitable for the proposed comparison.
Several kilometers of cumulative sliding distance are sufficient to induce the proposed surface evolution.
Sliding-induced surface deformation drives inverse Hall-Petch behavior that lowers near-surface shear strength and friction.
Sliding-induced deformation dynamically amorphizes the near surface.
The refined, high-energy near-surface microstructure accelerates formation of a stable passive film in NaCl solution.
The passive film lowers friction and wear by reducing direct metal-to-metal contact.
A dense passive oxide film inhibits electrolyte ingress and thereby improves corrosion resistance.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, the B-microalloyed AlCoCrFeNiMoTi variant will have lower friction coefficients and wear rates because of its refined surface structure.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, the microalloyed variant will exhibit higher corrosion potentials and lower corrosion current densities.
Under combined wear-corrosion conditions, total degradation will be lower than the arithmetic sum of degradation measured in isolated wear and corrosion tests.
The predicted protection will hold under moderate loading and corrosivity but diminish at extreme loads or electrolyte aggressiveness because the passive film may fail.
Failure to detect the proposed surface layer or stable passive film, together with failure to observe sub-additive combined degradation, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field identifies CoCrFeMnNi as the baseline material, whereas the baseline field defines the baselines as isolated wear-only and corrosion-only conditions. These are different comparison axes, leaving the reference for the claimed improvement inconsistent.
